chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the rattling/clattering of the Persians (non-Arabs) in the mosques.

key_terms.الْأَعَاجِم: The non-Arabs, specifically referring to the Persians in this context.
key_terms.رَطَانَة: Rattling, clattering, or noise; specifically referring to the sound made by Persians, often interpreted as their distinct way of speaking or moving that created noise.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet forbid regarding noise in mosques according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the Prophet’s prohibition of 'ratanah' (rattling or clattering noise) associated with the Persians (al-a'ajim) within mosques, reflecting the socio-cultural context of early Islamic architecture and the integration of diverse customs. Scholars interpret this as a directive to maintain the sanctity and tranquility of prayer spaces by avoiding disruptive, culturally specific noises that detract from spiritual focus. It underscores the principle of preserving the mosque as a place of solemn devotion, distinct from worldly distractions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah in Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Abu Sayyar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from talking gibberish (meaningless talk) in the Masjids’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from Misma’ abu Sayyar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, “The Messenger of Allah has prohibited speaking jargon language in Masjid (expressions understood by two people or a group only).’”
